prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Game-asset reference sheet for 3D modelling, wide landscape 16:9. Plain light neutral grey background, no scene, no sky, no clouds, no floating rock, no ground plane, a soft contact shadow only. Every piece fully isolated with clear space around it, nothing overlapping, nothing touching the edge, arranged in tidy rows, each with a small neat hand-lettered label underneath. MODULAR KIT PIECES sheet: Redraw of the attached reference sheet to the current spec: keep exactly the same pieces, their order, names and sizes. Ruin biome nature kit, 20 pieces, each drawn and labelled as its own piece, labels exactly as written in quotes, sizes as width x height. Row 1, TREES AND SAPLINGS: "Slab-splitter tree, broad" 9 x 8 m (gnarled light-brown trunk whose roots split a thick pale ruinstone slab and grip the halves, wide clumped yellow-green crown); "Slab-splitter tree, slender" 7 x 7 m (leaning twisted trunk, smaller higher crown, roots clasping two cracked slabs); "Root-gripped block" 3 x 3.5 m (toppled pale ruinstone cube engraved with a dead-teal channel and ring motif, a young tree's roots wrapping it, small crown on top); "Sapling in split block" 0.9 x 1.4 m; "Sapling in paving crack" 1.2 x 1.7 m; "Sapling among shards" 1.2 x 1.2 m. Row 2, IVY AND GROUND COVER: "Ivy clump" 1.3 x 1 m (rounded bush of five-lobed ivy leaves); "Trailing ivy" 0.7 x 1.8 m (one long hanging ivy strand, chunky leaf masses); "Joint grass tufts" 0.8 x 0.5 m; "Moss patch" 1 x 0.25 m (olive moss cushion with tiny white flowers); "Rubble scatter" 1.2 x 0.25 m (small precise pale shards and cubes). Row 3, RUINSTONE: "Perfect cube" 1.6 x 1.6 m (unnaturally smooth pale ivory-grey cube with engraved dead-teal channels and a ring motif); "Sheared slab" 1.6 x 1.1 m (thick bevelled slab sheared clean like cut glass); "Fallen ring segment" 2.4 x 2 m (toppled arc of a large square-section ring with a dead channel); "Cracked paving slab" 2 x 0.4 m (square flat slab cracked into pieces, channel and ring motif); "Shard rubble pile" 1.6 x 0.9 m (heap of precise pale shards, moss between). Row 4, ISLE EDGE: "Crumbling lip" 8 x 4 m (pale cracked paving with a dead channel crumbling over grey rock, broken slab ends, wilted orange grass on top, flat cut ends); "Paved lip" 8 x 4 m (intact clean edge of pale ruinstone paving over grey rock, a dead channel turning down the face, ivy over the edge); "Underside spire, large" 8 x 12 m (inverted tapering spike, pale ruinstone strata on top grading into faceted grey rock, dead dark-teal channel stepping down one face, hanging ivy); "Underside spire, small" 6 x 7 m (shorter, stubbier taper of the same rock). Draw only these 20 pieces: no floating fragments and no moss drapes. Pale ivory ruinstone, grey rock and yellow-green growth as in the attached sheet. Show each piece as an orthographic front elevation (no perspective) with a small three-quarter view beside it, on faint module grid lines, with its name and size (for example "3 x 4 m") in the label. Thick, solid forms, no thin parts. A plain neutral 1.8 m human silhouette labelled "1.8 m" stands on the sheet for scale, with everything at true scale to it. Title at the top: "Ruin nature kit".
